At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Departmental Overview
  
  

Founded in 1969, the Goldman School of Public Policy (GSPP) embodies the intellectual rigor, entrepreneurial spirit, public mission, and social commitment characteristic of UC Berkeley. As a professional school of public policy grounded in scholarly practice, GSPP mobilizes the campus's rich academic resources to provide a transformational academic and cultural experience that instills standards of excellence and a deep sense of pride in one's work, community, and academic home.
  
  

GSPP consistently ranks among the top policy schools in the country, currently ranked \#1 in policy analysis and \#2 in social policy by U.S. News \& World Report. Fundamental to GSPP's success is our culture, shaped by individuals from across the globe whose diverse perspectives and life experiences enrich our community. jobs.description:
Half the people who call themselves GTM engineers have never shipped production code. This job is for the other half.

**The Reality**
---------------


This is a software engineering role that happens to point straight at revenue. You'll write and ship production code, own the systems you build, and be measured by whether the revenue engine runs better because of your work. If your background is engineering that never got to touch the business, this is the role where it finally does. If it's been RevOps where you were quietly the most technical person in the org and nobody ever let you build properly, same.


We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. A company moving this fast catches its own mistakes sooner with the whole team in one room, thinking out loud at a whiteboard.


This will probably be one of the harder jobs you've had. It should also be one of the more interesting ones, because the revenue problems you'll be solving here will be the catalyst for our continued hyper growth.


Sound exciting? Good, we are too :)

**What We're Building**
-----------------------


Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales, built across Hyperbound Practice (AI roleplay), Hyperbound Perform (real call scoring and coaching), and Kota, our AI agent that acts on what we find. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.


Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23\), we're around 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

**The Role**
------------


You'll build the systems the go\-to\-market org runs on: lead routing and enrichment, pipeline and forecasting tooling, scoring and deal\-desk workflows, and the data layer that ties it all into one source of truth. This is production engineering: services and code you own, integrated across our CRM, product, and billing data, built to hold up as we scale. Where a no\-code tool is genuinely the right call, use it; the bar is that you can build the real thing when that's what the job needs.


There's a part of this job most GTM engineers never get. You'll dogfood Hyperbound on Hyperbound: our own reps run on Practice, Perform, and Kota, so the internal systems you build plug straight into the product we sell, and what you learn building them feeds back into the roadmap. You'll work closely with the founders and GTM leadership, act as part engineer and part systems designer for the revenue org, and have real say in what we build, not just how.

**The Team**
------------


We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and people who close. We've hired from our competition, brought on former founders, and pulled in early customers who loved the product enough to come build it.


The engineers here are builders first. Some have started their own companies. Nobody is precious about their code, and nobody hides behind "not my team's problem"; people see something broken and fix it. Someone is usually demoing something they shipped that morning, and the whiteboards get erased and rewritten all day. You can feel it when a team actually believes in what it's building, and that's very real here. It's also not a mattress\-under\-your\-desk startup: plenty of people have kids, people leave to make dinner, and they come back the next morning and ship. High standards don't require burnout.


We've doubled in size since this photo was taken a few months ago


When we close a real milestone we celebrate for real; after our Series A we took the whole team to Bali.

**Ownership and Equity**
------------------------


You own the outcome end to end: the systems you build, the revenue they move, and everything that happens after they ship. No process shields you from the responsibility, and none of it shields you from the credit either. Equity here is real, with real secondary opportunities, and we want the people who build this early to end up meaningfully rewarded for it.

jobs.description:
**About Town**
--------------


Town (town.com) is AI that starts from who you are. We build a persistent model of your identity, your voice, your judgment, your relationships, and your priorities, and use it to do real work on your behalf across every tool where you operate: email, calendar, documents, Slack, and more. Town doesn't wait for you to prompt it. It observes, learns, and acts. The more you use it, the more it becomes an extension of you.

  

Town was founded by Jean\-Denis Greze (CEO), former CTO of Plaid, and Tony Vincent (CPO), former Director of Applied AI Product at Google. We're a small, talent\-dense team backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Forerunner Ventures, First Round Capital, and Conviction, with more than $73M raised to date.

**About the role**
------------------


Town is building the most personalized, most capable AI assistant for everyone — and personalization at that level is a retrieval and data problem. The assistant is only as good as the context it can bring into the moment: the right memory, message, document, or relationship, pulled fast and related by meaning across everything a person and their team touch.


You'll build the foundation the whole product reasons over: the search and data infrastructure behind that context. One shared retrieval layer combining lexical and semantic search, the realtime and batch pipelines that keep it fresh and correct, and the durable data model everything else is built on.


This is greenfield and high\-leverage: you'll be the first person building this layer.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Build the search and retrieval layer that puts the right context at every Townie's fingertips, the moment it's needed — one shared layer the whole product pulls from instead of refetching context on its own.
* Combine lexical and semantic search and own the tradeoffs between them: vector vs. lexical, precompute vs. fetch, hybrid retrieval, and ranking.
* Design the durable data model the assistant's work is built on, so context is relevant, fast, and cost\-effective.
* Build and operate the pipelines behind it — realtime/streaming and batch — that keep the index fresh and correct as the underlying data changes.
* Stand up the indexing and storage layer and keep it fast and reliable at scale: latency, cost, freshness, and completeness.
* Lay the groundwork for relating content by meaning across everything the assistant knows — the start of a knowledge graph of people, companies, projects, and how they connect.

**You might thrive here if you...**
-----------------------------------

* Have significant, hands\-on experience across lexical and semantic search components and approaches (BM25, embeddings, ANN/vector indexes, hybrid retrieval, ranking).
* Have run large\-scale data infrastructure, ideally both realtime/streaming and batch — pipelines, indexing, and storage.
* Can make retrieval fast and cheap at scale, and reason about the latency, cost, and freshness tradeoffs cold.
* Are a systems thinker comfortable in greenfield, where the foundation doesn't exist yet.
* Are excited to take these systems from rapid prototype to production scale.
* Bonus if you've worked on ranking/relevance, knowledge graphs, or retrieval for LLM or agentic systems.

Half the people who call themselves GTM engineers have never shipped production code. This job is for the other half.

**The Reality**
---------------


This is a software engineering role that happens to point straight at revenue. You'll write and ship production code, own the systems you build, and be measured by whether the revenue engine runs better because of your work. If your background is engineering that never got to touch the business, this is the role where it finally does. If it's been RevOps where you were quietly the most technical person in the org and nobody ever let you build properly, same.


We're in the office five days a week in San Francisco. A company moving this fast catches its own mistakes sooner with the whole team in one room, thinking out loud at a whiteboard.


This will probably be one of the harder jobs you've had. It should also be one of the more interesting ones, because the revenue problems you'll be solving here will be the catalyst for our continued hyper growth.


Sound exciting? Good, we are too :)

**What We're Building**
-----------------------


Hyperbound is the Revenue Activation Platform and agentic operating system for sales, built across Hyperbound Practice (AI roleplay), Hyperbound Perform (real call scoring and coaching), and Kota, our AI agent that acts on what we find. We don't just record what happens on a call, we change what happens next.


Founded in 2023 out of YC (S23\), we're around 45 people now, Series A, $18M raised total. Last quarter we doubled headcount, revenue nearly doubled with it, and net revenue retention landed above 300%. Teams at LinkedIn, Workday, Vanta, and Intel run their sales orgs on us.

**The Role**
------------


You'll build the systems the go\-to\-market org runs on: lead routing and enrichment, pipeline and forecasting tooling, scoring and deal\-desk workflows, and the data layer that ties it all into one source of truth. This is production engineering: services and code you own, integrated across our CRM, product, and billing data, built to hold up as we scale. Where a no\-code tool is genuinely the right call, use it; the bar is that you can build the real thing when that's what the job needs.


There's a part of this job most GTM engineers never get. You'll dogfood Hyperbound on Hyperbound: our own reps run on Practice, Perform, and Kota, so the internal systems you build plug straight into the product we sell, and what you learn building them feeds back into the roadmap. You'll work closely with the founders and GTM leadership, act as part engineer and part systems designer for the revenue org, and have real say in what we build, not just how.

**The Team**
------------


We're assembling a cracked team of builders, operators, and people who close. We've hired from our competition, brought on former founders, and pulled in early customers who loved the product enough to come build it.


The engineers here are builders first. Some have started their own companies. Nobody is precious about their code, and nobody hides behind "not my team's problem"; people see something broken and fix it. You own the outcome end to end: the systems you build, the revenue they move, and everything that happens after they ship. Equity here is real, with real secondary opportunities, and we want the people who build this early to end up meaningfully rewarded for it.
